title: Historians reconstructed known Greek inscription text more accurately with Ithaca
location: Ancient Greek epigraphy research. Evaluator location unreported
observed_outcome: On masked known text, historians’ top-choice reconstruction accuracy was 71.7% with Ithaca, compared with 25.3% unaided.
human_contribution: Interpreted alternatives using historical knowledge and searchable textual parallels.
evidence_supports: The evaluation removed 1–10 known characters, allowing reconstructions to be checked against the original. Results are reported in Nature, Table 1.
limitations: Two trained evaluators do not represent all historians. Accuracy on masked known text does not establish accuracy on genuinely unknown text. The paper’s authors include Ithaca’s developers, and the corpus reflects prior scholarship.
tradeoffs: Incorrect reconstructions and uneven corpus coverage are considerations for future use. This record does not estimate their downstream effects.
replication_hypothesis: Test representative digitized corpora, expert interpretation, transparent alternatives, and independent contextual checks.
beneficiaries: Two graduate historians specializing in Greek history and epigraphy

sources.title: Restoring and attributing ancient texts using deep neural networks

source_case_identifier: Human reconstruction evaluation reported in Table 1
benefit_summary: On masked known text, historians’ top-choice reconstruction accuracy was 71.7% with Ithaca, compared with 25.3% unaided.
stakeholder_detail: The human evaluation involved two graduate specialists in Greek history and epigraphy. Wider benefits to scholarship or the public were not measured.
